cita: Wang et al. (2024). Agent Workflow Memory.
problema: LM-based web-navigation agents integrate only a fixed set of examples via training or in-context learning, so they lack robustness to changes in task context or environment and cannot learn from their own past successes and failures across a session to disentangle reusable task routines from increasingly complex tasks.
mecanismo: An LM-based induction module abstracts reusable 'workflows' (an NL description plus a step trajectory) from one or more agent experiences (WRITE), deliberately generalizing example-specific values into placeholders so routines transfer across instances; workflows are added to the agent's text memory (ADMISION) either offline (induced once from all training examples before test time) or online (streamed per test task, keeping only workflows from LM-judged successful trajectories, CONSOLIDACION), and complex workflows are built by composing/extending previously induced simpler ones.
evaluacion: Evaluated on WebArena (812 tasks, 5 websites, execution-based evaluation, online AWM) and Mind2Web (1000+ tasks, 200+ domains; offline + online AWM), against BrowserGym, SteP (human-written workflows), AutoEval, MindAct and Synapse baselines with GPT-4/GPT-3.5, plus cross-template/cross-website/cross-domain generalization splits.
numeros_clave: AWM improves WebArena overall success rate to 35.5% (+12.0 absolute / 51.1% relative over BrowserGym, and 7.6% relative over SteP's human-written-workflow baseline) while using ~2.0 fewer steps per task than BrowserGym and 40.8 fewer than AutoEval; on Mind2Web offline AWM reaches 4.0-8.9% relative and 0.4-2.8 absolute step/task success rate gains over Synapse/MindAct, driven mainly by +5.0-9.0 element-accuracy gains; cross-website/domain margins widen to 8.9-14.0 absolute points as the train-test gap grows.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the online setting only turns a completed trajectory into a workflow when an LM-judged evaluator marks it successful (§2.3), and later workflows explicitly reuse/extend earlier simpler ones (Fig.6), a direct example of promoting validated experience into durable, composable recipes.

AWM is measured head-to-head against retrieval of raw concrete examples (Synapse) and shows abstracted workflows beat concrete-example retrieval by +5.0 element accuracy (§3.2.1), external evidence that WHAT gets retrieved (abstracted vs raw) is a measurable design axis, not an assumed one.

reports steps-to-solve as an efficiency metric alongside success rate, showing AWM needs ~2.0 fewer steps than BrowserGym and 40.8 fewer than an evaluation-heavy baseline (§3.1.1), external evidence that memory-guided planning reduces interaction/token cost.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (WebArena), Table2 (cross-template), Table3 (Mind2Web offline), §3.1.1/§3.2.1.

cita: Jiang et al. (2024). Long Term Memory: The Foundation of AI Self-Evolution.
problema: Current LLMs are static, 'average' foundation models trained once and frozen at inference, so they cannot progressively personalize to an individual's or organization's long-tail data or continually improve from accumulated interactions without full retraining, which the authors argue requires a first-class Long-Term Memory (LTM) layer to enable inference-time 'self-evolution.'
mecanismo: LTM is proposed as a repository of refined, retained interaction data (WRITE) built and updated per specialized agent in a multi-agent architecture (MULTIAGENTE, the OMNE/AutoGen-based framework), where individual agents distill and store personalized knowledge that is periodically consolidated (CONSOLIDACION) into a shared collective memory model and updated in real time (ACTUALIZACION) as new interactions accumulate; retrieval combines RAG-style in-context retrieval with LoRA fine-tuning to locally update the model with LTM data (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) instead of always retraining all parameters.
evaluacion: Primarily a position/technical report; empirically grounds the LTM framework with an OMNE multi-agent system evaluated on the GAIA benchmark (400+ QA tasks) using GPT-4o + o1-preview with a scene-router deciding local-vs-web-tool solving, plus a cited Synthesis-Step-by-Step (S3) ablation on NLP task performance.
numeros_clave: Omne (the LTM-based multi-agent framework) achieved 1st place on the GAIA test set (40.53%) and 2nd place on the validation set (46.06%); a cited Synthesis-Step-by-Step (S3) ablation on smaller models' errors reports NLP task gains of up to 15.17%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: describes per-agent, cortical-column-like memories that are periodically merged into a shared LTM collective (§3.1, §6.3), external evidence for consolidating distributed transient experience into a durable shared store.

the OMNE architecture assigns each specialized agent its own memory slice, later integrated into a unified memory model (§6.3.1), a concrete multi-agent multi-store seam design relevant to MF's COSTURAS anchor.

the GAIA result (1st place, 40.53% test) is a genuine measured retrieval/tool-use benchmark, but the surrounding LTM framework (Sections 1-5) is argued conceptually rather than ablated against a no-LTM baseline, offering only partial support for MF's insistence on a measured retrieval layer.

notes: Numbers from §6.3.4 GAIA benchmark (Omne, 40.53%/46.06%) and the cited S3 ablation (up to 15.17% NLP gains).

cita: Liao et al. (2025). ReflecTool: Towards Reflection-Aware Tool-Augmented Clinical Agents.
problema: Clinical LLM agents are typically restricted to one narrow clinical scenario with a small fixed toolset, so they cannot generalize to a realistic, holistic evaluation across the diverse types of clinical data (images, EHRs, text, multi-document) and lack a mechanism to learn how to select and use domain-specific tools well from limited demonstrations.
mecanismo: An optimization stage lets the agent solve a small training subset with a clinical toolbox, self-reflects on each first attempt against the ground truth to produce a suggestion and a refined second trajectory, and only stores the refined trajectory in long-term memory when it succeeds (WRITE/ADMISION); successful vs. failed action usages are additionally compared to distill tool-wise experience per tool/action type (CONSOLIDACION); at inference the agent retrieves BM25-similar successful cases from memory (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) and applies the accumulated tool-wise experience via one of two verification methods -- iterative refinement or candidate selection -- to improve each tool call.
evaluacion: Evaluated on the newly introduced ClinicalAgent Bench (CAB, 18 tasks across 5 clinical dimensions) with Qwen2-7B/72B backbones against LLM/MLLM baselines and agent baselines (COT, ReAct, CRITIC, Reflexion), plus ablations removing long-term memory and tool-wise reflection, and a study of optimization-step count and verification size.
numeros_clave: ReflecTool surpasses the strongest agent baseline (Reflexion) by at least 3 points on CAB with both Qwen2-7B/72B, and surpasses the base LLMs by more than 10 points; ablation shows removing reflective long-term memory costs ~4 points (refinement) / ~7 points (selection) of average CAB performance (Table3); Candidate Selection already beats Iterative Refinement by ~4.5 points (62.5 vs 58) even before any optimization steps.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the ablation in Table3 isolates long-term memory and tool-wise action-level experience as separate levers and measures their individual contribution (removing memory alone costs ~4-7 points), direct evidence that consolidating validated trajectories into durable per-tool experience pays off measurably.

BM25-based case retrieval from long-term memory (Eq.5) is directly compared against no-memory ablations and against Reflexion's non-memory self-reflection, isolating retrieval's specific contribution to task success on a real benchmark.

the study of optimization-step count and verification size (Figs.3-4) trades more memory/compute for accuracy but is framed as a quality lever rather than a first-class token/latency cost measurement, relevant context but not a strong signal for MF's cost anchor.

notes: Numbers from Table2 (main CAB results), Table3 (ablation), Fig.3/4 (optimization-step and verification-size studies).

cita: Raman et al. (2025). REMI: A Novel Causal Schema Memory Architecture for Personalized Lifestyle Recommendation Agents.
problema: Personalized LLM lifestyle-assistant agents give generic, population-level advice because they cannot integrate a user's own multimodal life-event data into their reasoning, and even when they retrieve personal facts they surface correlations without an explainable causal chain linking a recommendation back to the user's own history.
mecanismo: A personal causal knowledge graph (nodes = life events/habits, weighted causal edges) serves as persistent long-term memory that is incrementally updated with new events (ACTUALIZACION, WRITE); a causal-reasoner module maps the query onto graph nodes via dual-encoder embedding similarity (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO), performs n-hop Graph-of-Thought/Tree-of-Thought causal traversal with LLM-based path scoring and counterfactual node-removal checks, followed by an LLM self-reflection validation pass (FIDELIDAD guard) before handing the validated causal factors to a schema-based planner that instantiates a matching plan template with the user's specifics, all glued together by an LLM orchestrator required to cite the causal trace and retrieved memory in its final explanation.
evaluacion: Evaluated qualitatively/quantitatively on 28 personal lifestyle scenarios (Gemini-2.0-Flash as orchestrator LLM) against a Memory-Only-LLM baseline (RAG-style, no causal reasoning) and an Ablated-CSM baseline (causal graph traversal but no schema planner), using two new embedding-similarity-based metrics: Personalization Salience Score (PSS) and Causal Reasoning Accuracy (CRA).
numeros_clave: On the afternoon-fatigue scenario REMI scores PSS 0.92/1.0 and CRA 0.60/1.0; across the 28 scenarios both baselines reach PSS 0.68-0.82 (comparable to REMI) but the memory-only baseline scores 0.0 CRA on every prompt while Ablated-CSM scores 0.2-0.6 CRA inconsistently, versus REMI's 0.4-0.8 CRA in every case.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: an LLM self-reflection loop revalidates each candidate causal factor before it informs planning, and a counterfactual verification step checks that a plan step actually severs the causal link it targets (§4.2.5, §4.3.3), a concrete grounding/staleness check on inferred memory before it is acted upon.

the system pairs a structured causal graph (in-memory networkx) with a separate FAISS vector store over unstructured logs (§4.4.1), a two-store seam design (structured causal facts vs semantic recall) relevant to MF's COSTURAS anchor.

Causal Reasoning Accuracy is measured against a Memory-Only (retrieval-only) baseline that scores 0.0 CRA on every prompt (§6), directly isolating what plain retrieval misses versus a measured causal-reasoning layer.

notes: Numbers from §6.1 (scenario walkthrough, PSS/CRA) and §6.3-7 (aggregate 28-scenario comparison).

cita: Wang and Chen (2025). MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents.
problema: Existing LLM agent memory systems store all history in a single flat, text-centric store (or a pure knowledge graph) with no routing into specialized memory types, so they retrieve inefficiently, fail on multimodal (image-heavy) input, and have no abstraction layer to keep storage bounded as raw screenshots or documents accumulate.
mecanismo: MIRIX routes incoming multimodal input into six typed memory components (Core, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Resource, Knowledge Vault) via a Meta Memory Manager that dispatches to six specialized Memory-Manager agents (MULTIAGENTE) which write and update (WRITE/ACTUALIZACION) their own memory type in parallel while deduplicating; Core Memory triggers a controlled rewrite when over 90% full (CONSOLIDACION-by-compaction); at query time an Active Retrieval mechanism first infers a topic from the query, then pulls top-K entries per memory type via embedding/BM25/string match (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO), tagging results by memory-type source for grounding (FIDELIDAD).
evaluacion: Evaluated on a new ScreenshotVQA benchmark (5,000-20,000 high-resolution screenshots per user, 3 users) against RAG and long-context baselines, and on the LOCOMO long-conversation benchmark (Chat Agent restricted to retrieved memory only, no raw transcript) against existing memory-system baselines.
numeros_clave: MIRIX achieves 35% higher accuracy than the RAG baseline on ScreenshotVQA while cutting storage by 99.9%, and a 410% improvement over long-context baselines with 93.3% less storage; on LOCOMO it reaches 85.38% overall accuracy, 8.0 points above the best existing method.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the six typed memory schemas (Core/Episodic/Semantic/Procedural/Resource/Knowledge-Vault, §3.1) each define explicit typed fields (e.g. event_type/summary/details/actor/timestamp for Episodic) rather than a flat text blob, a concrete instance of typed narrative memory MF's Tier-1 anchor could model closer to.

routing input to one of six specialized memory managers rather than one shared store (§3.3) is the paper's central design bet, and it is what drives both the accuracy gains and the 99.9% storage reduction, direct evidence for single-source-per-fact-type multi-store routing over a monolithic memory.

the headline ScreenshotVQA result explicitly pairs an accuracy delta with a storage-reduction delta (35% accuracy up, 99.9% storage down) rather than reporting accuracy alone, external evidence that a well-typed memory layer can jointly improve quality and cost.

notes: Numbers from §1 (main results, ScreenshotVQA and LOCOMO); memory schemas detailed in §3.1.

cita: Wong et al. (2026). Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases.
problema: Production-scale coding agents on massive repositories need both long-context reasoning (localizing and reasoning across dispersed modules without exceeding context limits) and long-term memory (accumulating reusable patterns and failure modes across sessions), but existing research-grade scaffolds use flat interaction histories or ad-hoc truncation/retrieval that silently drop important state, while production-grade systems trade away extensibility and interpretability.
mecanismo: A hierarchical, file-system-based working memory (a tree of Markdown documents with metadata tags) lets the orchestrator write/read/edit/delete state during a session (WRITE); an Architect Agent triggers adaptive context compression when the context nears a threshold, summarizing older turns into a structured plan (goals/decisions/errors/open TODOs) that replaces the raw history while keeping a rolling recent window (CONSOLIDACION+OLVIDO of raw turns, ACTUALIZACION of the compressed plan); separately, a note-taking agent distills each session's trajectory into persistent cross-session Markdown notes, explicitly including 'hindsight notes' for failures (errors, stack traces, abandoned strategies) that a later session retrieves (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) to avoid repeating the same mistake; a meta-agent automates a build-test-improve loop (MULTIAGENTE) that synthesizes and refines the orchestrator/tool configuration itself against a test set.
evaluacion: Evaluated on SWE-Bench-Pro (731 tasks) and SWE-Bench-Verified (500 tasks) across Claude 4/4.5 Sonnet, Claude 4.5 Opus and GPT-5.2 backbones against SWE-Agent, Live-SWE-Agent, and Anthropic/OpenAI's own proprietary scaffolds under identical repositories and tools; ablations isolate context management (hierarchical memory + compression) and meta-agent-learned tool-use versus a naive tool-use baseline.
numeros_clave: CCA reaches Resolve@1 59.0% on SWE-Bench-Pro with GPT-5.2 (vs OpenAI's own 56.0%) and 54.3% with Claude 4.5 Opus (vs Anthropic's own 52.0%); a weaker Claude 4.5 Sonnet + CCA (52.7%) beats a stronger Claude 4.5 Opus + Anthropic's proprietary scaffold (52.0%); ablation on a 100-example subset shows disabling context management drops Resolve@1 from 48.6% to 42.0% (Claude 4 Sonnet) and disabling advanced tool-use drops it from 51.6% to 44.0% (Claude 4.5 Sonnet).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: context compression explicitly replaces older raw turns with a structured plan (goals, decisions made, open TODOs, critical error traces, §2.2.1/Fig.3) that persists across turns as the agent's working state, a direct, measured instance of MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor (ablation shows disabling it costs ~6.6pp Resolve@1).

the note-taking system explicitly records 'hindsight notes' for compilation errors, exceptions, and abandoned strategies indexed by error signature so a later session retrieves the known fix instead of rediscovering it (§2.2.2), a direct implementation of negative-knowledge/re-derivation-avoidance memory.

the ablation table (Table2) isolates context-management and tool-use contributions to Resolve@1 on a matched subset, quantifying that scaffolding (memory/orchestration), not raw model capability, is a primary, measured determinant of quality under fixed compute.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main SWE-Bench-Pro results) and Table2 (context-management/tool-use ablation, §3.2-3.3).
